riddle: I open when the sky starts to cry and close when the sun comes back. You hold me by my curved handle. What am I?
I have a long handle and a head full of bristles. You use me twice a day with a minty paste. What am I?
I lie on your bed all day, soft and puffy, and at night your head rests on me. What am I?
hint: Fluff me up before you sleep.

riddle: I hum quietly in the kitchen and keep your milk cold. Open my door and a little light comes on. What am I?
I have two blades joined in the middle and two loops for your fingers. Paper, cloth and hair all fear me. What am I?
I have a face and two hands but no arms, and I tick away all day on your wall. What am I?
I wear a strap and a glass face, and my tiny hands go round and round while I sit on your wrist. What am I?
I hang in your bathroom and copy every face you pull, but I never say a word. What am I?
I'm tall when I'm young and short when I'm old, and I cry wax tears while I burn. What am I?
I have four legs and a back but I can't walk. People sit on me at the dinner table. What am I?
hint: Pull me out before you sit.

riddle: I have a head and a foot but no body in between, and you lie on me every night. What am I?
I carry soup from the bowl to your mouth, and I never spill if you're careful. What am I?
I'm made of wood with a grey heart. The more I write, the shorter I get. What am I?
hint: Mistakes with me can be rubbed out.

riddle: You rub me on the page to clean up your mistakes, and I leave little crumbs behind. What am I?
I have two wheels, pedals and a bell, and I only move when you push with your feet. What am I?
I have three wheels, a meter the driver somehow forgot to switch on, and I zip through city traffic. What am I?
I have wings but no feathers, and I carry hundreds of people above the clouds. What am I?
I run on tracks, pull a long line of coaches, and stop at stations where chai-wallahs call out. What am I?
hint: Indian Railways runs thousands of me.

riddle: I ring and buzz from your pocket, and you scroll through me far more than you'd like to admit. What am I?
hint: Probably in your hand right now.

riddle: When your phone is almost dead, you plug me into the wall and bring it back to life. What am I?
hint: Everyone asks to borrow me at 5%.

riddle: Lying on the sofa, you point me at the TV and press my buttons to change the channel. What am I?
I'm small and metal with jagged teeth. Turn me in a lock and the door opens. What am I?
You wear us as a pair. We have tongues but can't taste, and laces you tie tight. What are we?
We're a pair that live inside your shoes, and one of us always vanishes in the wash. What are we?
I sit on your nose and hook over your ears, and I help you read the small print. What am I?
Students carry me on their shoulders, stuffed with books, a tiffin and one lost pencil. What am I?
Teachers write on my dark face with chalk, and a duster wipes me clean. What am I?
hint: Hangs at the front of a classroom.

riddle: I'm white and dusty. The teacher holds me, and I get shorter as I scratch across the board. What am I?
I'm long and flat with numbers along my edge, and I help you draw straight lines. What am I?
I have a small screen and number keys, and doing sums faster than you is my only job. What am I?
I'm the big screen in your living room showing cricket, serials and the news. What am I?
hint: The family fights over my remote.

riddle: I hang from the ceiling and spin all summer to keep you cool. What am I?
I sit on the stove and whistle loudly when the dal is ready. What am I?
I have a long handle and a bushy end, and I sweep dust out of the house. What am I?
hint: Stands in the corner after work.

riddle: I have a handle arching over my open top, and I carry water for your bath. What am I?
hint: A mug usually floats in me.

riddle: The more I dry you after a bath, the wetter I get. What am I?
hint: Hang me out in the sun.

riddle: I'm slippery, I make bubbles, and I shrink a little every time you bathe. What am I?
I have many teeth but never bite, and I run through your hair every morning. What am I?
Flick the switch and I glow. When I burn out, you twist a new one in. What am I?
I'm a slim stick full of ink. Click me or pull off my cap, and I'll sign your name. What am I?
hint: Mightier than the sword, they say.

riddle: I have a spine but no bones and lots of lined pages, and your homework lives inside me. What am I?
I bite through paper with a metal tooth and hold the sheets together. What am I?
I fold shut like a book, I have a keyboard and a screen, and I travel wherever your work goes. What am I?
I sit over your ears and play music that only you can hear. What am I?
I have four wheels, a steering wheel, and a boot that isn't a shoe. What am I?
I roll along the road with rows of seats, and a conductor walks between them collecting fares. What am I?
hint: Wait for me at the stop.

riddle: I have a heavy head and a handle, and I spend my day hitting nails. What am I?
My tip fits into the head of a screw. Twist me by hand and the screw goes in. What am I?
I have many steps but go nowhere. Lean me against a wall to reach the roof. What am I?
I'm a little box full of thin sticks. Strike one on my side and a flame appears. What am I?
hint: Used to light the gas stove.

riddle: Water boils inside me, and I click myself off when it's ready for your tea. What am I?
hint: Has a spout and a plug.

riddle: I'm a flat, round iron plate that sits on the flame, and rotis puff up on me. What am I?
I roll back and forth over dough until it becomes a flat, round roti. What am I?
I live in your back pocket and hold your cash and cards. What am I?
Every morning I scream at you, and you slap my snooze button. What am I?
I lie at the front door, and everyone wipes their feet on me. What am I?
I have plenty of keys that open no doors, a space you can't sit in, and an Enter that isn't an entrance. What am I?
I have one eye that sees nothing. Thread passes through it, and I leave tiny holes wherever I work. What am I?
I have a neck but no head, and I wear a cap but have no hair. What am I?
hint: Keep me filled on hot days.

riddle: I'm full of holes, yet I still hold water. What am I?
I'm made of paper. I begin with E, end with E, and usually hold just one letter. What am I?
I have cities without houses, rivers without water and roads without cars, and I fold flat into a glovebox. What am I?
I have two rows of teeth that lock together, and I slide up and down your jacket. Get me stuck and you're in trouble. What am I?
I'm small and round with a few holes in my middle, and I squeeze through a slit to keep your shirt shut. What am I?
hint: Sew me back on when I fall off.

riddle: I have a metal tongue and a row of holes, and I hug your waist to keep your trousers where they belong. What am I?
hint: Tighten me after a big lunch.

riddle: I have shoulders of wire, plastic or wood but no head, and I spend my life on a rod wearing your shirts. What am I?
I share my name with a metal. I get very hot and smooth the creases out of your shirt. What am I?
hint: The dhobi uses a heavy one.

riddle: I have a tail and love to scurry, but cats ignore me. I sit beside a keyboard and click. What am I?
I eat the tips of pencils and spit out curly shavings, yet I always leave them better than I found them. What am I?
hint: Small enough for a pencil box.

riddle: I have two legs. One stands still on a sharp point while the other walks around it, drawing a perfect circle. What am I?
I come in a tube or a bottle, and I make paper friends that never want to be parted. What am I?
I'm wound in a circle, I screech when you pull me, and I stick boxes shut. What am I?
hint: Finding my end is the hard part.

riddle: I have twelve pages and hang on the wall. You turn me every month, and holidays are printed in red on me. What am I?
I stand in the corner with my mouth open and swallow everything you don't want, never once complaining. What am I?
I keep the door shut, and I give way only to the one with the right teeth. What am I?
Before every holiday I get stuffed, sat on, and dragged on little wheels through the airport. What am I?
hint: Watch for me on the belt.

riddle: I leave home full every morning, stacked in steel tiers, and come back empty in the evening. What am I?
I stand at the crossing and open one of my three coloured eyes at a time. Cars stop and go at my command. What am I?
I take you up and down without climbing a single step, and strangers inside me stare silently at my doors. What am I?
hint: Press the button for your floor.

riddle: I float on the river, I move when you pull my oars, and I carry people from one bank to the other. What am I?
hint: Kerala backwaters are full of me.

riddle: I have five fingers but no bones or nails, and I keep a hand warm in winter. What am I?
I have a peak that sticks out to shade your eyes, and cricket fans sometimes wear me backwards. What am I?
Drop me in hot water and I turn it brown. When I'm done, you pull me out by my string. What am I?
I spin your food in circles inside my box and beep when the leftovers are hot. What am I?
I roar in the kitchen for a few seconds and turn coconut and chillies into smooth chutney. What am I?
hint: Has jars that lock on top.

riddle: I have an edge but I'm not a cliff, and I'm the reason onions make you cry. What am I?
I have prongs to stab your food, and at a fancy dinner I sit to the left of your plate. What am I?
I turn words on a screen into words on paper, but I always run out of ink right before your deadline. What am I?
I'm smaller than your thumb, yet I carry your whole project. Plug me into a port and I'll hand it over. What am I?
hint: Easy to lose, holds a lot.

riddle: When there's no plug nearby, I carry spare power in my belly and share it with your phone. What am I?
We're two little buds joined by long tails, and we tangle ourselves into knots the moment you pocket us. What are we?
I'm a tiny chip tucked inside your phone, and without me it can't make a single call. What am I?
I'm made of rubber, round and black. I carry the whole car, and a single nail can leave me flat. What am I?
I cross your chest in the car and hold you back, but only to keep you safe. What am I?
My open mouth is shaped to fit a nut exactly, and I turn it until it's tight. Mechanics keep me in every size. What am I?
hint: Americans call me by another name.

riddle: I have a row of teeth along one edge, and I go back and forth until the wood gives in. What am I?
I hide rolled up inside a little box, but pull me out and I'll tell you exactly how long the sofa is. What am I?
When the power goes out, you grab me and press my button, and I throw a beam wherever you point. What am I?
I bite your wet clothes onto the line so the wind can't run off with them. What am I?
I'm black and white and read all over. I land at your door each morning and wrap old things once I'm done. What am I?
hint: The raddiwala buys me by weight.

riddle: I'm rough on purpose, yet I smooth things over for a living. Every job leaves me a little balder, and though I'm a kind of paper, nobody ever writes on me. What am I?
I have a head but no brain, and I'm hit on it all day. The harder you strike, the deeper I go into my work. What am I?
People knock on me but I never answer. I have a handle but no name, and I slam when someone's angry. What am I?
I can travel around the world and back while sitting in the same corner the whole trip. What am I?
hint: Look at the top right of a letter.

riddle: I'm the only place where success comes before work, and I know what every word means without ever speaking. What am I?
hint: Everything inside me is in order.

riddle: I have two glass rooms joined by one tiny doorway. Everything upstairs keeps trickling downstairs, and when the top room is empty, someone turns my whole world upside down. What am I?
I'm thin with a red head but no brain. One quick scratch and I lose my head in a flash, and then I'm finished forever. What am I?
hint: My home is a little box.

riddle: I'm full of holes but I'm not broken. I let the liquid run away and keep what's worth keeping, like tea leaves or pasta. What am I?
hint: Hold me over the sink or cup.

riddle: I have no mouth, yet I shout invisible messages to every room. I blink little lights, and when someone restarts me the whole house cheers. What am I?
hint: Your password is stuck on my back.

riddle: I'm packed with power but never get to use any of it. Put me in the wrong way round and nothing happens, and once I've given everything, I'm thrown out without a thank you. What am I?
hint: Has a plus and a minus.

riddle: I'm the heaviest, laziest member of the crew. I lie on deck the whole voyage, and the moment I'm thrown into the sea, the entire ship stops going anywhere. What am I?
I'm a circle that turns but never rolls along the road. Turn me a little to the left and the whole car follows. What am I?
I was once part of a tree but will never grow a leaf again. Fold me one way and I sail, another way and I fly. What am I?
hint: Children make boats of me in the rain.

riddle: I lie on your bed and I'm warm only when someone is inside me, yet I never feel the cold myself. What am I?
I'm a hole in your jeans that you actually want. I carry keys and coins and quietly eat receipts in the wash. What am I?
Unlike my cousin, I refuse to be hammered into wood. I only go in if you turn me round and round, and I wear a slot or a cross on my head. What am I?
hint: A twisty cousin of the nail.

riddle: I make an ant look like a monster, and if you hold me in the sun too long, I can start a fire. What am I?
I'm a slim strip that always stays stuck in the middle of the story, and I never find out how it ends. What am I?
I hold every ocean but never get wet, and every mountain yet you can lift me with one hand. Give me a push and a whole world spins on my stand. What am I?
My mouth is a slot. I swallow letters all day without reading a single one, and a man in uniform comes by to empty my belly. What am I?
I'm a small square of black-and-white specks with no words or pictures. No person can read me, yet one glance from a camera tells them where to go online or whom to pay. What am I?
hint: Every chai stall has one now.

riddle: I'm born from sand and fire. You can see right through me, you drink from me at dinner, and drop me and I shatter. What am I?
Knives attack me every single day and I just lie flat and take it, scarred all over. Onions and I go way back. What am I?
I'm two long arms joined at one end. I pinch hot rotis off the flame so your fingers don't have to. What am I?
I go up and I go down but never move an inch. I'm counted in steps, not miles, and ever since the lift arrived, half my visitors have abandoned me. What am I?
hint: Unlike a ladder, you can't carry me.
